articles.title: 5 reasons why Wall Street added $1.5T today
articles.summary: US stock market today, 9 November, 2026: Wall Street has added $1.5 trillion in market value, but the biggest surprise is where investors are putting their money. Semiconductor stocks are recovering, Tesla is climbing and oil prices are falling. The Dow Jones has gained more than 1,000 points, while the S&P 500 is up 2.17% and just 4% away from a record high. Yet Nvidia is falling nearly 5%.Monday's US stock market rally: Here's 5 reasons why Dow Jones, S&P 500 and Nasdaq are rallying today1. AMD stock jumps 12% as investors return to semiconductor stocksAdvanced Micro Devices (AMD) is leading the semiconductor recovery. Its shares jumped more than 11% during Monday's trading and later extended gains to more than 12%, according to the latest November 9 update.The rally has two important drivers. First, investors are buying chip stocks after last week's heavy sell-off. Second, Oppenheimer upgraded AMD to Outperform from Market Perform and set a $600 price target.The company's growing AI business and its Google Cloud partnership are also supporting investor interest. AMD's rebound is particularly important because chipmakers were among the biggest losers during last week's technology sell-off.2. Tesla stock rises 5.45% as Magnificent Seven stocks recoverTesla (TSLA) shares climbed 5.45% to $377.74 in the November 9 market snapshot. The recovery reflects renewed buying across major technology companies after weeks of losses.Meta Platforms also gained around 5%, while Apple (AAPL) rose 2.16% to $349.77. Alphabet, Amazon and Microsoft advanced more than 2%.These companies have significant weight in major US stock indexes. Their gains are helping the Nasdaq and S&P 500 recover. Tesla's rise also suggests investors are looking beyond semiconductor stocks for opportunities in the technology sector.3. Nvidia stock falls nearly 5% as Jensen Huang investigation unsettles investorsNvidia (NVDA) is moving in the opposite direction. Its shares fell 4.98% to $177.34 in the supplied midday snapshot, despite the broader technology rally.The pressure follows reports concerning CEO Jensen Huang and Alice Huang, a Singapore-based business executive reportedly suspected of gathering information for China. Jensen Huang acknowledged an extramarital relationship and said he would cooperate with the investigation.Nvidia's board has launched an independent investigation. The company has said it has no reason to believe that national security or its business secrets were compromised.4. Broadcom and Marvell stocks jump more than 8% as AI chip demand returnsBroadcom (AVGO) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) each gained more than 8% on Monday. Intel (INTC) and Micron Technology (MU) also moved higher.The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) climbed more than 6%, showing that the recovery extends across the chip industry.Investors are returning to semiconductor companies after last week's selling raised questions about AI investment, data centre construction and future chip demand.However, the recovery does not mean those concerns have disappeared. Investors will continue watching technology companies' capital spending plans and demand for AI infrastructure.5. Constellation Energy and Barrick Mining stocks gain as earnings support Wall StreetConstellation Energy (CEG) shares climbed around 8%, while Barrick Mining (B) advanced approximately 4% following their quarterly results.Constellation is attracting attention because of its role in supplying electricity to data centres. Rising demand for computing power has made electricity availability an important part of the AI investment story.Barrick's gains also show that Monday's buying is not limited to technology companies. Investors are finding opportunities in other sectors as market sentiment improves.Why are oil prices falling while gold rises?Crude oil is another important part of Monday's market movement. WTI crude futures fell around 3.2% to $87.90 per barrel, while Brent declined approximately 4%.Investors are watching developments in the Iran war and the possibility that tensions could ease. Lower oil prices can reduce fuel costs for businesses and ease some inflation concerns.Gold moved in the opposite direction, rising 1.5% to around $4,140 an ounce. Bitcoin traded near $75,000 after retreating from weekend levels above $76,000. The 10-year US Treasury yield also moved higher to approximately 4.89% from Friday's 4.87%.Can the S&P 500 reach a new record high?Monday's rally comes after a difficult four weeks for Wall Street. The S&P 500 lost 5.6% over that period, while the Nasdaq Composite declined 10.2%. Both indexes recorded four consecutive weekly losses, their longest losing streaks since March.The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had reached record highs on October 6. The S&P 500 is now around 4% below its previous peak.

articles.title: All about Nvidia CEO Huang's affair controversy
articles.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship with a business executive suspected by US intelligence of gathering information for Beijing, as the chipmaker's board launched an independent investigation into reports that its founder was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. While Huang has apologised to his family and company employees saying he was ‘unfaithful’ to his wife, Nvidia said it has no reason to believe that US national security or the company's secrets were compromised.US President Donald Trump has defended Huang, describing him as an "honourable guy" who has done an "amazing job" for the country. Trump also expects Huang to remain at the helm of Nvidia, adding that the executive deserved to have his side of the story heard.Also read: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's secret affair: Why did US intelligence suspect Alice Huang of spying for China?The controversy follows reports by The New York Times and the Financial Times that US intelligence agencies had identified a close relationship between the Nvidia leader and Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman associated with Singapore-based data centre company Megaspeed. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she was gathering information for Beijing.Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang issues key statementIn a draft email to Nvidia employees, Huang acknowledged having an extramarital relationship, "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did.”In a separate message reported by The New York Times, he apologised to his family and company employees, taking responsibility for his actions. "I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it," he wrote.Addressing Nvidia employees, Huang also acknowledged that he had fallen short of his responsibilities towards them. “My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to Nvidia and will work to earn back your confidence," he said.He also requested privacy for his family, saying they bore no responsibility for his choices.Huang has not directly addressed the allegations that the business executive, aka, the Chinese spy was gathering information for the country. He has, however, supported Nvidia's investigation and committed to cooperate with it.Also read: Nvidia opens probe into CEO Jensen Huang over affair with woman suspected of spying for ChinaNvidia announces independent investigationNvidia's board of directors announced an independent investigation following reports that Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors, assisted by external independent legal counsel.In its statement, Nvidia said, "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or NVIDIA secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information." The company added that the board prioritised US national and economic security, which it said was paramount to Nvidia and its shareholders.The board also expressed confidence in Huang and his leadership team and said it would provide further updates as appropriate.Huang, 63, will continue as Nvidia CEO during the investigation, it clarified.Speaking on Huang meeting thousands of customer executives every year, the company previously said that it regularly receives updates from the US government regarding parties and entities of concern and acts accordingly.Trump defends Nvidia CEOTrump has publicly defended Huang amid the controversy, describing him as an honourable person and praising his contribution to the US."I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on," Trump told reporters. "I think he's an honourable guy," he said, adding that Huang had "done an amazing job for our country".When asked whether Huang should remain Nvidia's CEO, Trump replied: "I think so. Sure."Trump also suggested that Huang should be given an opportunity to explain himself. Asked whether he would take Huang on his planned trip to Asia, Trump said, "I don't know, but I'd certainly take him."The remarks came amid reports that Trump had been briefed on intelligence findings concerning Huang's relationship with the Chinese businesswoman roughly a year ago but had chosen not to act on the information, according to The New York Times.The Financial Times separately reported that a US government memo based on intelligence information about the alleged relationship had been shared with a small group of senior US officials shortly before Trump travelled to Beijing for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping.The FT also reported that Trump had held multiple meetings with Huang since beginning his second presidential term in 2025. Huang had personally lobbied Trump earlier this year to allow Nvidia to export its H200 chips to customers in China.Who is Alice Huang, the Chinese spy?Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese national and former senior executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data centre company.According to The New York Times, Alice Huang was previously a television reporter in China before becoming a senior executive at Megaspeed. The company buys equipment powered by Nvidia chips and rents computing capacity to businesses, including Chinese technology company Alibaba.US intelligence agencies reportedly concluded that Alice Huang had developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang and was passing information directly to Beijing.The Financial Times reported that the US intelligence community believed she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security, the country's main intelligence agency.Jensen Huang had previously described their association as a normal business relationship.Megaspeed and its connection to the Nvidia caseMegaspeed has come under US scrutiny over concerns that Nvidia's advanced AI chips may have been diverted to China.The New York Times reported that Megaspeed had been examined for potentially steering Nvidia AI chips to China. According to the publication, the firm bought more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the past two years.The Financial Times reported that Megaspeed was spun off from a Chinese gaming company in 2023. US authorities have been investigating companies, particularly in Southeast Asia, suspected of helping China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export restrictions.Nvidia had previously launched an internal investigation into allegations concerning the diversion of chips through Megaspeed but assessed that there was no evidence of wrongdoing, according to the Financial Times.US lawmakers step up actionSenior Republican lawmakers in the US House of Representatives earlier asked Huang to brief Congress about the allegations and Nvidia's security protocols.In a letter dated November 4, Brian Mast, chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee; John Moolenaar, who leads the China Select Committee; and Eric Crawford, chairman of the Intelligence Committee, sought a closed-door briefing from Huang on November 18.The lawmakers sought answers about the New York Times report and Nvidia's security protocols against foreign adversary espionage. The letter said the allegations raised significant national security concerns regarding China's access to sensitive US technology and information.The lawmakers added that Congress needed to determine the extent to which US national security had been placed at risk.Meanwhile, Chris Coons, a Delaware Democrat who is due to chair the Senate Foreign Relations Committee from January, pledged to open an investigation."Congress will investigate and get answers," Coons wrote on X, referring to what he described as the relationship between the Trump administration, Chinese spies and AI billionaires.Political and corporate reactions to Jensen Huang affairUS Secretary of State Marco Rubio declined to comment on the allegations when asked about the report, describing it as an "internal corporate matter", according to AFP.Technology analyst Dan Ives of investment bank Yorkville Ives described the investigation as a "black eye moment" for Huang. Ives said the controversy could trigger multiple congressional inquiries and create an overhang on Nvidia's stock.He also warned that the development could increase scrutiny of the company's chip sales to China, which remains a key issue in Washington.Huang's position at Nvidia could also come under scrutiny depending on the outcome of the board's investigation, Ives said, adding that the CEO's importance to the company's global strategy made the controversy a risk for the stock.Separately, Elon Musk responded to a social media post about the controversy. The post suggested that while Huang had done something incredibly foolish, there might have been no malicious intention. Musk replied, "I agree."Nvidia stock downNvidia shares came under pressure in out-of-hours trading following the announcement of the board investigation.Perpetual futures trading on the Hyperliquid exchange and after-hours shares trading on the Blue Ocean system showed Nvidia shares at around $180.30 on Monday, down approximately 3.4% from Friday's Nasdaq closing price of $186.64.The development has raised concerns about the potential impact of the controversy on investor sentiment, particularly given Huang's importance to Nvidia's business and its global AI strategy.South Korean govt intervenes in Nvidia CEO caseSouth Korea stated that Nvidia's contracted GPU deliveries to the country are expected to proceed without disruption despite the controversy surrounding Huang.Vice Science Minister Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee on Monday that 10,000 GPUs funded under a 2025 supplementary budget had already arrived and were in use. GPUs planned for 2026 were under contract and expected to enter service this year."We expect production and the delivery schedule for contracted volumes to proceed without disruption," Ryu said, adding that the ministry was monitoring developments and discussing prices and schedules with Nvidia Korea.Meanwhile, a planned visit to South Korea by Huang's daughter Madison Huang, an Nvidia senior director, was cancelled.South Korean AI startup Rebellions said her planned visit to its headquarters and a dinner with partners had been called off due to unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia.Kakao Mobility also cancelled a photo session and question-and-answer event with her. However, the company said its business agreement with Nvidia would proceed, with senior director Gaurav Agarwal attending instead.Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to attract around 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, was proceeding as planned, according to South Korean media.The investigation's findings, the response from US lawmakers and any further developments concerning Megaspeed's business dealings with China will be key to determining the wider implications for Nvidia.

articles.title: Chandra and Mehli reconnect at Tata HQ
articles.summary: Mumbai: Fresh from Italy, where Tata Motors announced the acquisition of commercial vehicle maker Iveco, Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran invited Mehli Mistry, the late Ratan Tata's confidant and a trustee of the Tata Education and Development Trust, to Bombay House on Thursday.Coming just days after the two were seen together at the wedding celebrations of Mehli's daughter Laila, the meeting reinforced a belief within Tata circles that relations between the two are improving after more than a year marked by a broader power shift within the Tata Group following the death of Ratan Tata.Also read: Plea seeking Tata Sons listing filed in Bombay High CourtPeople familiar with the matter said Chandrasekaran and Mehli, who was voted out of the two principal trusts that hold majority in Tata Sons by Noel Tata and others, discussed issues that had affected their ties.Mehli-Chandra meet focused onrebuilding trust, restoring equationMehli's challenge against his removal is pending before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC).Mehli and Chandrasekaran's conversation last week was focused on rebuilding trust and restoring a working equation. Mehli later left for Dubai, with both sides appearing keen to move beyond a difficult period in one of Tata Group's most significant internal relationships.For much of the past decade, Mehli and Chandrasekaran were regarded as allies. After the dramatic ouster of Cyrus Mistry as chairman of Tata Sons in 2016, Mehli played a key role in the legal fight that followed between Cyrus and Ratan Tata. When Ratan Tata had to choose a successor, he picked Chandrasekaran, assisted by Mehli. Mehli later backed Chandrasekaran's second and third terms as chairman of Tata Sons. The third term, however, became contentious after Noel Tata, who succeeded Ratan Tata as chairman of Tata Trusts, opposed Chandrasekaran's reappointment.Mehli and Chandrasekaran's relationship survived differences in personality and style. Those who know Mehli describe him as intensely loyal, fiercely independent and refreshingly blunt. Friends admire his willingness to say in a room what others prefer to whisper outside it. Critics point to a temperament that can run ahead of diplomacy. The redeeming feature, according to people who have worked closely with him, is that his anger rarely lingers.Also read: Noel Tata proposes splitting Tata Sons as alternative to RBI-mandated listingChandrasekaran is a different kind of leader. Publicly measured and understated, he has cultivated the image of a consensus-builder since arriving at Bombay House. Yet colleagues say beneath that calm exterior lies a highly competitive executive with sharp political instincts and an acute understanding of institutional power.Then came the post-Ratan Tata era. Ratan Tata's death in Oct 2024 altered the balance of influence within Tata Trusts. Disagreements that had previously been settled privately soon surfaced within the trusts.Mehli and fellow Tata Trusts trustees Darius Khambata, Pramit Jhaveri and Jehangir Jehangir argued that information on Tata Sons covered under Article 121 of the company's Articles of Association had not been shared with them, limiting their ability to take informed decisions. The four trustees voted Vijay Singh off the Tata Sons board.Concerns about the emerging situation prompted a visit to Delhi by Noel, Tata Trusts vice-chairman Venu Srinivasan, Khambata and Chandrasekaran, who briefed senior government officials on governance issues within the trusts.Mehli, who was inducted into Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) and Sir Ratan Tata Trust (SRTT) by Ratan Tata and remained one of his most trusted advisers, increasingly found himself at odds with the emerging power structure. He was eventually voted out of the two trusts by Noel, Srinivasan and Singh, who is also a vice-chairman of the trusts.Among the relationships most affected was Mehli's equation with Chandrasekaran. Differences emerged over how developments within the trusts were characterised and communicated to external stakeholders, with Mehli maintaining that his interventions were driven by governance concerns. Communication between the two subsequently became infrequent.People said Chandrasekaran later made efforts, through intermediaries and directly, to reopen channels of communication with Mehli. Mehli remained a respected figure among trustees, a prominent voice within the Parsi community and an influential presence in discussions concerning the Tata legacy.Mehli has challenged the end of his trusteeship before the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner (MCC), where the matter is pending. He, however, never withdrew his support for Chandrasekaran's stewardship of Tata Sons. In filings before the MCC, he said he had backed Chandrasekaran's reappointment for a third five-year term and was a signatory to the resolution approving it.Chandrasekaran's second term as chairman ends in Feb 2027. His third term is linked to his continuation as a director of Tata Sons, which requires the trusts' approval at the company's annual general meeting (AGM). However, Tata Sons was unable to hold its AGM on Aug 18 after it failed to secure the requisite quorum. articles.title: Sheikh Hasina about to return to Bangladesh?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ousted Bangladeshi Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested on Monday a new passport and identity card so she can return from self-imposed exile in India, according to a letter seen by Reuters, her first such communication since fleeing in 2024.The request marks the clearest step by Hasina to act on her plan to return to Bangladesh in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising ended her long rule, raising the prospect of fresh political and legal tensions in a country where her party is now banned.Also read | G7 allies to assess impact of Trump's midterm setback at Paris talksShe has told Reuters she plans to return to surrender before a court, and her aides said on Monday the date would be announced once various formalities were completed. Bangladesh's war-crimes court sentenced her to death in November last year in her absence for ordering a deadly crackdown on the student-led uprising, though she has denied the charges from exile."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers wrote to Preeti Rahman, acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi.The letter asked for the applications to be processed "expeditiously" on the basis of her Bangladeshi nationality and in accordance with "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".Rahman in Delhi and spokespeople for Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in Dhaka did not immediately respond to requests for comment.Also read | Trump says his deportation policy 'might have been too tough' for votersHasina's Awami League party was the country's largest before it was banned following her fall. Many of her party colleagues have either been jailed or are in self-imposed exile in India or elsewhere.Having ruled Bangladesh for 20 years as prime minister across multiple terms, Hasina still enjoys support among sections of the population, and a return could sharpen political divisions as the government in Dhaka seeks to restore stability after more than two years of upheaval.On the other hand, it could improve Bangladesh's strained ties with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave her refuge.

FCNR(B) interest bill to keep dollar hedging costs high
articles.summary: Mumbai: A multibillion-dollar FCNR(B) interest bill, coupled with the Reserve Bank of India's new reserve requirement on forex derivatives, is likely to keep dollar hedging costlier for Indian banks, treasury executives said.While the RBI provided a hedging facility for the $133 billion raised for three to five years under the special window opened for mobilising foreign currency deposits, banks must bear the currency risk on interest payments to non-resident depositors.135667176At an average interest rate of 6.5-7.0%, the annual interest outgo on these deposits is estimated at $8.6 billion to $9.3 billion. At least half of this amount remains unhedged, according to treasury heads at six banks ET spoke with, leaving lenders with more than $4 billion in dollar exposure to manage annually."The interest on FCNR(B) deposits is not covered by the window. Banks have to buy those dollars forward themselves, year after year, in the open market," said Anindya Banerjee, head of currency research at Kotak Securities.Read more: Bonus, stock splits & dividends: Dabur India, HUL, ONGC among 76 companies turning ex-record date this week"A forward premium is simply the extra price one pays today to lock in dollars for delivery later. When the entire banking system is buying dollars forward for the same reason, and there are not enough natural sellers, that extra price goes up," Banerjee said.Adding to the pressure is the RBI's new reserve requirement on banks' derivative positions. Introduced on October 10, the foreign exchange risk reserve (FERR) requires banks to maintain a cash reserve equivalent to 20% of the rupee value of eligible foreign-exchange derivative contracts.FERR makes it more expensive for banks to offer certain forward-dollar hedges because they must lock away cash against the contracts. Banks may pass on part of this additional cost to customers, putting further pressure on forward premia. The one-month and one-year forward premia were 2.50% and 2.78%, respectively, in early August. They surged to 8.50% and 4.85% by mid-October before easing to 3.83% and 3.91% by November 6, reflecting near-term dollar demand.A treasury head from a private bank said most banks had not put a hedging strategy in place as they were still assessing how best to manage this exposure. FERR in October added another layer of cost, making banks more cautious about locking in dollar liabilities over longer tenures. He explained that for now, the exposure was managed as it accrued, using short-term contracts that could be rolled over rather than hedging the entire interest obligation upfront. The reliance on short-term, rollover, contracts means banks will repeatedly return to the forward market as their interest liabilities accrue, sustaining demand for dollars instead of eliminating the exposure through an upfront hedge.Read more: Market may deliver bumper returns by next Diwali as valuations and earnings align, says Raamdeo AgrawalForeign banks, however, appear more comfortable carrying unhedged positions because they receive a steady stream of dollars from clients.A treasury executive from a foreign bank said some banks might hedge in the coming days as the rupee appreciated.The rupee staged a sharp recovery during the week, appreciating nearly 1.2% to close at 93.90 per dollar on Friday, its strongest level in more than six months.Some midsize banks, meanwhile, hedged the bulk of their dollar exposure after costs fell within their internal thresholds.

articles.title: Bengal's push to bring workers home raises concerns in Keralam
articles.summary:
Building contractor Vijayakumar is keenly awaiting the return of his expert worker, a native of Murshidabad district in West Bengal, after he left for home to celebrate Durga Puja. Only, the worker's return remains uncertain now.
The uncertainty stems from an appeal by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari asking workers to stay back, citing livelihood opportunities under the VB-G RAM G scheme, which guarantees 125 days of work and enables them to earn a livelihood while living with their families.

He is an expert in building houses in the traditional Keralam style, according to Vijayakumar, from Veliyanadu village in this district.
